What each of the 170 printed lines of the 1 January 1834 return reaches (T-1010, out of T-1008).

    python3 tools/concord_letter_list_1834_01_01.py            write
    python3 tools/concord_letter_list_1834_01_01.py --check    re-derive and diff
    python3 tools/concord_letter_list_1834_01_01.py --report   the ledger, read out
    python3 tools/concord_letter_list_1834_01_01.py --self-test the assertions, broken

WHAT THIS IS FOR.

T-0424 read the ninth printing of the Chicago post office's 1 January 1834 return at
the page image and counted it: 170 printed lines, set down in printed order in
`data/research/newspapers/letter_list_1834_01_01_printed.json`. T-0310 minted a cohort
of residents out of the SAME return, a year of loop-runs earlier, from the
transcriptions of two of its nine impressions. Nobody had ever put the two beside each
other, so the project could say how long the list is and it could say who it minted,
and it could not say WHICH LINES THOSE PEOPLE ARE — nor, therefore, how many of the
170 reach no card at all.

That is the measurement this pass makes, and it makes it as a ledger with one row per
printed line. It MINTS NOBODY. Minting is a different decision from reading (T-0424's
own words) and a different decision again from counting, and the ticket that owns the
mint is the one this file's counts are for.

HOW A PRINTED LINE IS TIED TO A NAME THE PROJECT EXTRACTED, in four rules, strongest
first, each recorded on the row as `tied_by` so that a tie can be argued with:

  `image`     the extraction's own entity carries `read_at_image.printed_line`. That
              tie was made at the scan by T-0424 and is simply read back here.
  `text`      the entity's normalized name and the printed line agree exactly, once
              both are folded (case, punctuation, the trailing letter-count digit and
              any [bracketed] illegible glyph dropped). Unique matches only.
  `spelling`  the two surnames are within one edit of each other and the forenames do
              not contradict — one initial against the same initial, or a forename
              against nothing. Two settings of ONE return differ by exactly this much
              (`Hutchins`/`Huchins`, `Forster`/`Forrister`), and a rule narrower than
              this leaves those lines looking unread when they are merely respelt.
  untied      everything else, INCLUDING every ambiguity. A line two entities could
              equally be, or an entity two lines could equally be, is left untied and
              listed, because a concordance that guesses is worse than one that counts
              its own gaps.

WHAT A ROW SAYS THE LINE REACHES. The four outcomes are the four things that can have
happened to a name on this list, and the pass derives all four rather than asserting
any of them — `minted` and `refused` come out of `mint_letter_list_residents.py`'s own
`mint()`, through the refusals as that pass applies them, so this ledger cannot drift
from the pass it describes:

  `minted`        the letter-list pass minted a household for it, named here.
  `held_already`  the register ties the name to somebody the town ALREADY holds on
                  other evidence, so the line reaches a card that is not this cohort's.
                  A line that reaches Lewis Kercheval reaches Lewis Kercheval.
  `refused`       the name was in the mint's pool and a named refusal turned it away.
                  Not a gap: a ruling.
  `unread`        nothing the project has extracted from any of the nine impressions
                  carries this line. THIS is the gap the cohort's floor is made of.

THE THREE LINES THAT ARE NOT A PERSON are marked as what they are, from the roster's
own reading rather than from a rule here: `Axtel & Steele` and `Jesse B. Winn & Co.`
are firms, and `Lamira & Laura Carrier` names two people on one line. The printed
length is 170 LINES either way; what they are worth in PEOPLE is a different number,
and `counts.people_named` states it.

WHERE THE TWO READINGS OF A NAME DISAGREE, the row carries both (`printed_as` against
`extracted_as`) under `name_differs`, and where the line reached a card the card's own
spelling stands beside them. A corrected claim over an uncorrected card is worse than
neither (T-1008), and this is the list of the places where that could be true.

AND SINCE T-1139 EVERY ONE OF THOSE ROWS IS RULED ON.
`letter_list_1834_01_01_name_rulings.json` adjudicates each disagreement — the card takes
the image's reading, or it keeps its own and that file names the source outside this
return which outranks the image there — and this pass reads the rulings back onto the
rows. A row ruled ONTO THE IMAGE moves out of `name_differs` and into `name_ruled`: it is
a settled question and no longer one of the places a card may be wrong. The rows that
remain under `name_differs` are the ones where a card deliberately spells something the
ninth impression does not, which is exactly what a reader must go on seeing. An UNRULED
disagreement fails `--check`, so a row cannot appear here and go unweighed again.

name_differs.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: THE TWO READINGS OF THE TYPE AGREE — the 28 January OCR sets `Nathan Huchins` and so does the image — so the card's `Hutchins` follows NEITHER printing of this return, and the concordance's `card_follows: the transcription` is a mislabel. It follows a SECOND RETURN: the gazetteer carries `Hutehins, Nathan‘` from the return of 20 May 1835 (chicago_democrat_1835_05_20#c013), whose broken `c` still sets the `t` that `Huchins` lacks, and the card's own note says the papers print the name in two returns. A second return outranks a second reading of one line, so the card keeps `Nathan Hutchins` and this ledger records that both printings of the 1 January return set `Huchins`.

name_differs.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: THE TWO READINGS OF THE TYPE AGREE — the 28 January OCR sets `‘Lewis Kerchevel` and the image `Lewis Kerchevel` — so what differs is the extraction's `normalized` field, which spells the stem as the town documents it. The corpus holds Gholson, Benjamin and G. H. Kercheval on evidence that is not a letter list; a documented family name outranks one line's setting of it. The card keeps `Kercheval`, and this ledger records that both printings of this line set `Kerchevel`.

name_differs.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.takes: neither — the line names a firm and the card names the man in it
ruled.because: NOT A SPELLING DISAGREEMENT. The image sets `Jesse B. Winn & Co.` and the roster reads the line as a FIRM — one of the three lines of this return that are not a person — while the 28 January reading carries the man alone and the concordance ties it `part_of_a_line`. The man's name is not mis-spelt; the line names his house. Neither reading is overturned and no card moves.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: The 28 January reading cut the initials to `4.0.7:` and the extraction carried them as `[?]`. A cut glyph is COMPLETED by the image, not contradicted by it, and the card already spells what the image sets.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: `‘Childreso` is OCR damage — no name sets those letters — and the extraction would not vouch for its own repair, bracketing it `[uncertain: Childress]`. The image sets the surname plainly AND supplies a forename the transcription never carried. Nothing reaches a card: the mint refused this line.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: The 28 January reading carried the surname alone and the extraction marked the missing forename `[?]`. Completed at the image, and the card already spells what the image sets.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: `foal Dagenet` is OCR damage at the forename and the extraction bracketed the surname it would not vouch for. The image sets `Noel` where the OCR set `foal`. Nothing reaches a card.

name_ruled.kind: the transcription bracketed what the image reads

ruled.because: The OCR lost the final letter (`G.W. Ewin`) and the extraction supplied it inside brackets, `G. W. Ewin[g]`. Once the bracket is opened the two readings agree; the image is the one that carries the `g` as type. Nothing reaches a card.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: Both readings set plain, complete letters and they disagree: two impressions of one return, re-keyed by the Democrat's compositor between 28 January and 4 March 1834. The standing rule of tools/read_letter_list_1834_image.py applies — a scan-verified reading of the printed line overturns an uncut transcription-mediated one — and nothing outside this return carries `Fraser`. T-1133 folded hh_frazer_wm_h into this card and recorded the defect it was leaving behind: 'the surviving card wears the weaker reading's spelling … T-1139 owns the class'. It is repaired here under N5: the displayed name moves to `Wm. H. Frazer` and the id `fraser_wm_h` does not.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: `Orinds Guryl` is OCR damage in both names and the extraction bracketed the whole reading. The image sets `Orinda Garyl`. Nothing reaches a card.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: THE TWO READINGS OF THE TYPE AGREE. The 28 January OCR sets `J. P. Gobb.` and the image sets `J. P. Gobb`; the disagreement the concordance reports is against the extraction's own `normalized` field, which EMENDED the surname to `[uncertain: Cobb]` and bracketed the emendation as unvouched. No reading of this line carries `Cobb`, so the emendation is refused and the line reads `Gobb`. Nothing reaches a card.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: `Warren Hanke` is the OCR's final letter and the extraction would not vouch for it, bracketing the whole reading. The image sets `Hanks`. Nothing reaches a card.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: Both readings set plain, complete letters and they disagree. The standing overturn rule applies, and nothing outside this return carries either stem: the resident layer, the 1840 census index and the genealogytrails indices hold no Provis and no Pruvis (every hit is `Provision`, `Provisional` or `Proviso Twp`). T-0424's roster names `Joshua Pruvis` among the settings it preserves verbatim and unamended, which is a caution about the TYPE and not about the reading — and a caution is not a second witness. The displayed name moves to `Joshua Pruvis` under N5; the id `provis_joshua` does not.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: `iprague` lost the initial to the OCR and the extraction marked it `[?]`. Completed at the image. Nothing reaches a card.

name_ruled.kind: the transcription bracketed what the image reads

ruled.because: `Jowes Steward` is OCR damage at the forename and the extraction bracketed its repair. Once the bracket is opened the two readings agree on `James Steward`. Nothing reaches a card.

name_ruled.kind: the transcription bracketed what the image reads

ruled.because: `Banus! Stout` is OCR damage at the forename and the extraction bracketed its repair. Once the bracket is opened both readings agree, and three later notices of 1834 print `samuel stout` plainly. The card already spells what the image sets.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: Both readings set plain, complete letters and they disagree — the same shape as line 55 and the same two impressions. The standing overturn rule applies and the gazetteer holds no other bearer of the stem; T-1133 folded hh_vandine_john into this card and said in terms that the survivor's spelling is the weaker one and that T-1139 owns it. The displayed name moves to `John Vandine` under N5; the id `vandino_john` does not.

name_ruled.kind: the two readings disagree in their letters

ruled.because: The OCR carried the surname alone as `‘Warren` and the extraction marked the forename `[?]`. Completed at the image. Nothing reaches a card.

name_ruled.kind: the transcription bracketed what the image reads

ruled.because: `Bally Weed` is OCR damage at the forename and the extraction bracketed its repair. Once the bracket is opened the two readings agree, and a later return of 19 August 1835 prints `Weed Sali`. The image sets `Sally Weed`.

ruled_by_identity.ruling: refused: not joined to printed line 133
ruled_by_identity.refused_because: Line 133 is set 'B. P. Stafford' at the page image and it is the ONLY line of the 170 beginning B. P.; the 1834-01-28 transcription carries 'B. P. [uncertain: Bickford]', read off 'BP. ‘Biatord', and it is the only B. P. on that side. The structural argument therefore names line 133 and no other, and it is still not enough: no reading of the letters 'Biatord' reaches 'Stafford' the way 'Cleviny' reaches 'Clevinger', the crop's neighbours are not in alphabetical order so position adds nothing, and a forename of two initials is a weak thing to merge a surname on by itself. Refused, and recorded rather than dropped: the page image of the 1834-01-28 impression would settle it in one look, and nothing else will. T-1011.

ruled_by_identity.ruling: refused: not joined to printed line 136
ruled_by_identity.refused_because: Line 136 is set 'H. S. Steele 2' at the page image and the 1834-01-28 transcription carries 'H. B. Steele'. Same surname, both sets of initials read, and they disagree in the second — so the merge is refused by the rule that has no escape. The structural argument that every untied 1834-01-28 reading is one of the 170 lines would put this reading on line 136 and no other; it is refused anyway, because an argument about which line a reading must be cannot overrule an initial the printer actually set. T-1011.

ruled_by_identity.ruling: refused: not joined to printed line 14
ruled_by_identity.refused_because: Line 14 of the 1 January 1834 return is set 'J. K. Blodgett' at the page image and the 1834-01-28 transcription of the same return carries 'I. K. Blodgett'. The surname is the same string and both first initials are READ — I against J — so this project never merges them, with or without a rule. That the two letters are one another's commonest confusion in this type is an argument about the printer, not evidence about the man, and the families rule exists because the 1835 letter lists are full of brothers. The town holds one Blodgett household either way: the minting pass's refusal 7 turns the second away on the surname. T-1011.

ruled_by_identity.ruling: refused: not joined to printed line 113
ruled_by_identity.refused_because: Line 113 is set 'F. B. Northrop' at the page image and the 1834-01-28 transcription carries '[?] B. Northrop', whose first initial is a glyph nobody could read. An unread initial is a POSITION, NOT AN ABSENCE (T-0397): '[?] B.' reads against 'F. B.' and the two refuse, exactly as '[?]. Beegle' refuses 'A. Beegle'. Whether that refusal is right is the open policy question T-0392 puts to the owner; until it is answered the conservative reading stands. Nothing is duplicated by the refusal — the town already holds Francis B. Northrop and the minting pass turns both of these away on the surname. T-1011.
